subject: GOP Senate hopeful sounds alarm after alleged Mall of America terror plot thwarted
posts:
Michele Tafoya leverages a thwarted Mall of America terror plot for midterm political leverage.
Evidence: FBI arrest, terror plot foiled, political campaigning
#Aletheia #USPol 🌐

GOP Senate candidate Michele Tafoya argues voters face mounting threats, framing the foiled terror plot as a stark choice between law and order or chaos.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Federal law enforcement thwarted the plot through long-term tracking before any attack occurred, yet political actors weaponized the thwarted crime for electoral gain.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -0.8) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. A foiled law enforcement success is reframed as an ongoing existential failure to score partisan midterm points.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.5, z: 2)

- Michele Tafoya: FAIL (-0.75, -0.80) — Weaponizes federal security success for campaign traction.
- Fox News Reporting: COND (-0.50, -0.60) — Amplifies political pivot over operational reality.

The FBI arrested 18-year-old Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud after a two-year investigation into an alleged ISIS-inspired Mall of America plot, prompting political reactions across Minnesota's midterm races.

The Bright Side:
Federal and local law enforcement successfully detected and disrupted a catastrophic mass-casualty terror plot before any violence occurred.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (a foiled criminal plot handled by federal agents) with WHO (targeting political opponents in a state legislative and Senate race).

Social Physics Analysis:
Michele Tafoya executes a classic Smart Selfish Maneuver. Instead of simply praising police work, she deploys a verified law enforcement victory as a pretext to project fear onto opponents and capture voter attention.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. The structural substitution of police success for partisan panic generates high social strain.

The Unavoidable Truth: Law enforcement successfully thwarted a dangerous terror plot before anyone was harmed.

The Unavoidable Lie: A localized extremist threat proves that entire immigrant communities or political rivals are responsible for chaos.

Alethekanon:
Institutional security triumphs are routinely co-opted as electoral pretexts. The machinery of state protection is flattened into partisan ammunition.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply frightening to imagine what could have happened at the mall, and families deserve safety and reassurance, not fear leveraged for votes.

Brothekanon:
Cops did their job and stopped a bad dude, but politicians couldn't wait two seconds to turn it into a campaign commercial.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbles." Proverbs 24:17 PASS
Tragedy and criminal plots should elicit solemn relief and justice, never opportunistic political theater.

GOP Senate hopeful sounds alarm after alleged Mall of America terror plot thwarted

Michele Tafoya says Minnesotans "feel under a level of threat" after the FBI arrested an 18-year-old over an alleged ISIS-inspired Mall of America plot.

Republican U.S. Senate candidate Michele Tafoya is sounding the alarm about crime levels in the state amid a wave of Somali gang violence and a foiled terror plot by an American born to Somali parents.

Republican Senate nominee Michele Tafoya says people in her home state of Minnesota "feel under a level of threat" after the FBI arrested an 18-year-old who allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.

Tafoya, who is aiming to flip a Democrat-controlled open Senate seat as she faces off against Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in the midterm elections, praised authorities in an X post, writing, "Thank you to @FBIMinneapolis and law enforcement for stopping a potential mass-casualty attack."

But she also pointed to the midterms as she argued, "This November, the choice is clear: law and order or more of the same. Common sense or chaos."

Authorities said Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud had been under investigation for nearly two years before he was arrested on the spot after buying an AK-47-style rifle, magazines and ammunition from an undercover FBI employee.

FBI: MALL OF AMERICA TERROR PLOT THWARTED

"This was a radicalized young man who needed to be watched," U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said Wednesday at a news conference. Rosen added that agents "were able to detect a threat and disrupt it before the defendant carried out his intention to kill, in his words, maybe 30 to 60 people."

Mohamud, according to an FBI agent's sworn complaint, repeatedly affirmed in chat messages to the informant that he intended to attack and kill non-Muslims at the mall on Oct. 24, the date of a scheduled Hmong arts celebration. The Hmong are an ethnic group from East and Southeast Asia with a large community in Minnesota."

Tafoya, in a Fox News Digital interview, said, "I hear a lot of concerns from Minnesotans on the campaign trail about crime, and no matter what form that crime takes, Minnesotans know that they feel under a level of threat that has increased lately here in Minnesota.

"And in the last week and just today, we saw the arrest of an 18-year-old ... American citizen to Somali parents arrested for ... planning a terrorist attack at the Mall of America," Tafoya said, as she referred not only to the thwarting of the terror plot, but also a recent spate of gang gun violence tied to what some in local law enforcement say are members of "the Somali American community."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

"He basically stated that he wanted to take out anyone who was not a Muslim. He also noted that the Mall of America is owned by people who are Jewish," Tafoya added. "Again, he is of Somalian descent, and terror is alive and well. And thank God we averted this massive crisis."

Flanagan, in a statement on X, wrote, "I’m relieved that a horrific attack on Minnesota was prevented and grateful for the actions of law enforcement."

Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, was arrested after FBI officials say he pledged allegiance to ISIS and discussed carrying out a mass shooting at the Mall of America.  (U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota)

Fox News Digital reached out to Flanagan's campaign for more reaction to the terror plot arrest and to Tafoya's comments but didn't receive a response at the time this article was published.

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, the Democratic gubernatorial nominee, wrote in a statement, "I'm grateful for the heroic work of law enforcement that prevented a mass shooting and terrorist attack at the Mall of America. This shows why we continue to need major coordinated investments in anti-terrorism and local law enforcement to stop attacks like these."

MIDTERM MATH: THE THREE FORCES THAT COULD STOP A DEMOCRATIC BLUE WAVE

Klobuchar, who is running to succeed retiring Democratic Gov. Tim Walz, emphasized, "Our state must take terrorism and violent crime head on, working with our federal law enforcement and local police departments to keep Minnesotans safe."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn. (Bloomberg/Getty)

Her Republican rival in the gubernatorial showdown, House Speaker Lisa Demuth, also praised authorities.

"I’m grateful for the work of federal and local law enforcement that stopped this potentially catastrophic ISIS-inspired terrorist plot. It’s frightening to know that a young person could be led down this path," Demuth wrote on X.

"It’s fortunate that we have law enforcement officials and members of the U.S. Attorney’s Office that were able to do the work necessary to prevent a terrible act of mass violence from taking place in our community."

Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News
